newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military team sent to Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military team sent to Brazzaville.

text.p: A small U.S. military assessment team was flown to troubled Brazzaville in the Congo on Tuesday to assess the situation in case an evacuation of Americans is requested, the Defence Department said.

Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon said the team of about a dozen communications specialists, security troops and planners arrived in the Congolese capital on Tuesday afternoon. He stressed that no decision had been made on any evacuation.

Bacon said there were believed to be about 60 Americans in Brazzaville including some 15 workers at the U.S. Embassy, which remained open despite reports of heavy gunfire among warring factions in the city.
"The situation there is quite chaotic now," he said, adding that there had been no request from the U.S. Embassy to remove Americans.

Bacon said the U.S. military team arrived from Germany on a C-130 military transport plane and that some Americans would be taken out on that plane. He praised French troops in the city for helping provide security and evacuating some Americans.
He told reporters that any evacuation from the Congo was likely to be handled by U.S. Special operations forces in aircraft from Europe.
